title: Michigan signs up Coke, Meijer, Google for first in-stadium advertising at Big House
content:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan Stadium, which turns 100 next year, is getting ads for the first time in its history.

Coca-Cola, Meijer and Google Gemini will be the first three sponsors to display their logos inside the 107,601-seat Big House, Michigan announced Wednesday. The school released renderings of the sponsors’ ads on the sides of the video board, the wall at the base of the stands and the national championship sign on the south side of the stadium.

“Michigan Stadium is one of the most iconic and cherished venues in all of sports, and we have been deeply intentional about preserving its tradition, character, and identity,” athletic director Warde Manuel said in a release. “As we introduce this partner program, we will do so with care and purpose, ensuring that any brand partner presence is strategic, tasteful, and aligned with the values of the University of Michigan.”

The sponsor logos likely will be integrated into other aspects of the in-stadium experience, including programming on the video board, spokesman Dave Ablauf said. Before this season, sponsor logos appearing in the stadium included the Allstate field goal nets, the Gatorade logo on sideline equipment, the Michigan Medicine logo on the injury tent and the Jordan Brand logo on players’ jerseys.

Michigan previously announced it was exploring in-stadium advertising, field logos and jersey patches as a way to generate additional revenue for player compensation. Ohio State recently announced a jersey patch deal with Chase Bank worth around $17 million, and Notre Dame announced a similar deal with SoFi worth up to $20 million per year. Michigan has yet to announce a jersey patch sponsor.

Michigan projects $297 million in athletics revenue and expenses for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The school reported $35.6 million in corporate sponsorships, advertising and licensing on its 2025 NCAA financial report. That number ranked third nationally behind No. 1 Texas ($52 million) and No. 2 Ohio State ($42.8 million).

Michigan reported $175.3 million in football revenue for 2024-25, joining Notre Dame and Texas as the only schools at more than $170 million. No figures were available for the financial impact of the in-stadium advertising, Ablauf said.

— Matt Baker contributed to this report.
